name: Parallex
description: Parallex is a prefrontal cortex modulator that suppresses the brain's natural bottleneck in attentional switching, allowing users to genuinely maintain multiple independent cognitive threads simultaneously rather than rapidly alternating between tasks. In BCI-augmented individuals, it allows conscious awareness to be distributed across multiple simultaneous data streams, processes, and physical tasks without degradation. It is the standard pharmaceutical for network operators, air traffic analogues, and multi-system engineers.
effects: True parallel cognitive processing (2-4 simultaneous task threads)
Sustained performance across multiple concurrent workstreams
Reduced error rate in complex multi-variable environments
side_effects: Difficulty converging on single-task focus post-dose
Identity fragmentation at high doses — threads feel like separate selves
Fatigue is masked during dose, crashes severely after
Mild dissociation from physical body sensations
Long-term: baseline attention becomes permanently fragmented
cultural_context: Parallex is the quiet workhorse of GLMZ's knowledge economy. Network operations centers, logistics hubs, and emergency dispatch services run on it. The identity fragmentation side effect is poorly understood and underreported — users describe it as 'becoming the job' and struggle to remember who they are outside of work contexts. On the street, bootleg patches called 'Hydra' are worn by Shelf hustlers managing multiple illegal operations simultaneously.
story_hooks: A Novafold network operator has been on Parallex patches for three years solid — they can manage 40 simultaneous systems flawlessly, but they've lost the ability to have a single coherent conversation or sustain a personal relationship
A Shelf fixer running multiple jobs simultaneously is wearing bootleg Hydra patches — and one of the 'threads' in their head has started making decisions the rest of them didn't agree to

A corporate saboteur needs to simultaneously manage a physical infiltration, a BCI hack, and a cover story — Parallex is the only way, but they've never used it before and the identity fragmentation hits during the job
